clue.text: Test paper solution

parts.note: reads as the answers to an exam paper, but means the dye solution used to soak the paper chemists use to test for acid

explanation.surface: Someone wants the answers to an exam they are sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'test paper' is the chemist's indicator paper, not an exam, and the 'solution' is the liquid dye it is soaked in.
explanation.definitionFit: This lichen dye, turning red in acid and blue in alkali, is made up as a solution and soaked into indicator paper.

clue.text: Sinister bass player

definitions.meaning: in heraldry and Latin, sinister means on the left
on a piano the lower notes are played by one particular hand

explanation.surface: A menacing musician plays the bass guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' is the Latin and heraldic word for left; a pianist's left hand plays the bass part.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for left, and a pianist's left side handles the low bass notes.

clue.text: Instrumental call of the wild ?

parts.note: names a brass instrument and also the loud cry an elephant gives in the wild

explanation.surface: Echoing Jack London, the summons of nature is played on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls Jack London's novel; the elephant's cry shares its name with the brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument shares its name with the bellowing cry an elephant makes.

clue.text: Don has double trouble, not being initiated

indicators.note: trouble means disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A university lecturer is in twice the difficulty for not being admitted to a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges DON and DOUBLE together; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds not yet blooded have had no first kill, so the word means inexperienced or not yet initiated.

clue.text: Retainer helping to ensure a safe flight

definitions.text: Retainer helping to ensure a safe flight

parts.words: Retainer helping to ensure a safe flight
parts.note: the retainer is not a servant but a metal bar holding a carpet in place, and the flight is a staircase, not an air journey

explanation.surface: A loyal servant helps make sure an air journey goes off safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft; it is a flight of stairs, and the 'retainer' is the bar that holds the carpet against each step.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal bar fixed across the base of each step keeps a staircase carpet in place so nobody slips.

clue.text: ESP to save our proverbial penny ?

definitions.text: ESP to save our proverbial penny ?

parts.words: ESP to save our proverbial penny ?
parts.note: extrasensory perception would spare us paying the penny offered in the saying 'a penny for your thoughts'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether telepathy could save money.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverbial penny is the one in 'a penny for your thoughts': if you could read minds you need not pay it.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrasensory perception includes telepathy, knowing what is in another person's mind without being told.

clue.text: Key colour

definitions.meaning: piano keys were traditionally faced with elephant tusk

explanation.surface: A crucial shade for a designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were faced with elephant tusk, and that material's creamy white is a named shade.

clue.text: Giant of the Russian forest ?

parts.note: in Cold War slang a Soviet Russian is a Red
a wood is a small forest

explanation.surface: A huge figure lives in the forests of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'giant' is a tree: the Californian sequoia, among the tallest living things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian sequoia is among the tallest trees on earth, a true giant of the forest.

clue.text: Viewpoint of some top people

parts.note: seems to be the opinion of an elite, but means a window projecting from a sloping roof, through which attic dwellers look

explanation.surface: The opinion of certain leading figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewpoint' suggests opinion; it is literally a place to look out from, used by people living at the top of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set vertically into a sloping roof gives attic rooms their outlook.

clue.text: Sporting activity going to church?

parts.note: horse racing over jumps took its name from cross-country races run towards a distant church spire as the goal

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a sport on the way to church.
explanation.walkthrough: The jump race took its name from early cross-country races ridden towards a church spire visible on the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing over fences and ditches began as cross-country chases with a distant spire as the finishing point.

clue.text: With which a rifleman pulled through — making eight?

definitions.text: With which a rifleman pulled through — making eight?

parts.words: With which a rifleman pulled through — making eight?
parts.note: the strip of flannel a soldier draws through the rifle barrel to clean it, named for its size in inches, and a multiplication whose product is eight

explanation.surface: A rifleman survived a crisis, and something helped him come through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled through' sounds like recovering; a 'pull-through' is the cord and cloth drawn down a rifle barrel to clean it. The cloth's dimensions, multiplied, make eight.
explanation.definitionFit: British army rifle-cleaning flannel was cut in pieces four inches by two, and four times two is eight.

clue.text: Bath in succession ?

parts.note: the Bath is a British ... of knighthood, and things in succession are arranged one after another, in sequence

explanation.surface: People take turns to use the bathtub, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is not the tub or the city but the Most Honourable Order of the Bath, a British chivalric honour; 'in succession' means in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bath is a knightly order, and a sequence of things one after another is an arrangement or order.

clue.text: Support for the flavour of beer

definitions.text: Support for the flavour of beer

parts.words: Support for the flavour of beer
parts.note: sounds like backing a taste, but means the tall stake that the climbing plant used to flavour ale grows up

explanation.surface: Someone is campaigning in favour of the taste of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' suggests approval; it is a physical prop for the climbing bine whose cones give beer its bitter flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter cones that flavour ale grow on climbing bines trained up tall stakes in Kentish gardens.

clue.text: Stay to take your peg out

definitions.text: Stay to take your peg out

parts.words: Stay to take your peg out
parts.note: a stay is a supporting line, and here it runs out from a tent to its peg in the ground

explanation.surface: A guest is told to stay so that they can take their coat off its hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb, remain; it is a noun, a supporting line, and the 'peg' is a tent peg it is stretched out to.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is held up by taut lines, or stays, running out to pegs driven into the ground.

clue.text: Famous memo to the end of the world

parts.note: a memo is a short written note

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word world is taken and added on

explanation.surface: A notorious memo predicts the end of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrated or well known is distinguished in their field.

clue.text: Play put on the map

definitions.meaning: freedom of movement, leeway or scope
the lines of north-south position drawn on charts and globes

explanation.surface: A theatrical production is staged somewhere notable.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway or scope is one sense; the other is angular distance north or south of the equator, marked as parallels on maps.

clue.text: Bit of a fiddle bringing up the rear

definitions.meaning: a part of a violin, the piece the strings are anchored to at the bottom
coming at the end, as a closing section or ornament

explanation.surface: A small swindle comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Violin strings are fixed to a part at the bottom end; the word also means a final piece or appendix.

clue.text: Submitted for what the contractor did

definitions.meaning: handed in, as a bill or account
a builder coats a wall with plaster or cement

explanation.surface: A bill was sent in for the builder's work.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is handed over or submitted; and a builder coats walls with plaster, a job also called by this word.

clue.text: Source of worry affecting people at the top

definitions.text: Source of worry affecting people at the top

parts.words: Source of worry affecting people at the top
parts.note: seems to describe the stresses of senior management, but literally describes a pain in the topmost part of the body

explanation.surface: Something troubling the bosses of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People at the top' suggests leaders; read literally it is pain in the top part of everyone, the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A nagging problem is colloquially a pain in the skull, and such a pain afflicts the topmost part of anyone.

clue.text: Letter shows fibre is under the record

indicators.note: in this down clue the fibre is placed beneath the record

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
istle is a plant fibre from Mexican agave

explanation.surface: A letter shows that some fibre lies beneath the record.
explanation.walkthrough: ISTLE is a tough fibre from agave plants; in a down clue 'under' sets it below EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written message, as in the books of the New Testament written to early churches.

clue.text: She could be Queen of Paris

indicators.note: says the letters of the French word may be rearranged into a different form

parts.note: the French word for a queen is reine, as Parisians would say it

explanation.surface: A woman might be the queen of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word REINE, from 'Queen of Paris', is rearranged ('could be') into a woman's name; 'She' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, of Greek origin meaning peace, so a female could bear it.

clue.text: Form of spell that is broken

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A kind of magic incantation has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SPELL with IE; 'of' is a link and 'Form' means a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval shape, a closed curve such as a planet's orbit, is a geometric figure or form.

clue.text: Arms cuts

definitions.meaning: weapons, long spears used by mounted knights
surgeons open boils by slicing into them

explanation.surface: Weapons inflict wounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Long spears carried by cavalry are weapons; and a surgeon opening a boil makes an incision.

clue.text: Oriental hero, the Prophet's son-in-law, takes the cake

parts.note: Ali married Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad
a baba is a rum-soaked yeast cake

explanation.surface: A celebrated Eastern figure, related by marriage to the Prophet, helps himself to the dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' joins the two pieces; the hero is the woodcutter of the Arabian Nights tale with the forty thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcutter of the Arabian Nights who outwits forty thieves is a hero of Eastern storytelling.

clue.text: Tree contributes to the general derision

indicators.note: contributes to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tree adds to everyone's mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A birch-family tree common by rivers and wet ground.

clue.text: Spotted notes about item that made Isaac think

indicators.note: the two notes stand around the fruit, one on each side of it

parts.note: D is a musical note, here taken twice
Isaac Newton is said to have thought of gravity when an apple fell

explanation.surface: Someone noticed jottings concerning the thing that set Newton thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'noticed' but is the definition, meaning marked with spots; 'about' puts D and D around APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with patches of colour, like a horse with mottled markings.

clue.text: Quoted as having sound vision

indicators.note: the clue word sound says the answer is a word pronounced the same as another

parts.note: having vision means being able to see, sighted

explanation.surface: Someone is quoted as possessing clear-sighted judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound vision' looks like good eyesight; 'sound' is the homophone signal on 'having vision', SIGHTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote a passage or authority is to refer to it by way of evidence.

clue.text: Landlord has stronghold in target area

indicators.note: the tower is put inside the target ring

parts.note: the inner is the ring of a target just outside the bull
a keep is the fortified central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A property owner keeps a fortress in a zone under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The landlord here runs a pub rather than letting property; 'in' is the container signal, and the inner is the ring of an archery target next to the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: The licensee who runs a pub is called its landlord in Britain.

clue.text: Year of the Ox of course?

definitions.text: Year of the Ox of course?

parts.words: Year of the Ox of course?
parts.note: a young bullock's years, read as two words, and also the action of guiding a vessel's course

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether this is naturally the Chinese Year of the Ox.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chinese zodiac is a red herring: a steer is a young ox, so its years are its 'steer age', and 'of course' points to steering a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiding a ship on its course is the act of steering; the word also splits as a bullock's years.

clue.text: Top command for Arnold perhaps

definitions.meaning: to top is to cut off the head
an order telling Thomas Arnold, the famous Rugby School headmaster, to take charge as headmaster

explanation.surface: Arnold receives the most important order of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arnold was the celebrated nineteenth-century headmaster of Rugby School, so he could be told 'Be head!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping someone means decapitating them; split as two words it orders someone to serve as headmaster.
